issue.title: Lvalue `optional<NonMovable>` does not satisify `view`, but is `viewable_range`

discussion.p: The C++26 marked all specializations of `optional` as the view (`enable_view` is `true`), however, for type `M` that is not `movable`, optional<M> does not satisfy the `view` concept.

Generally, overstating support in opt-in is accepted and unharmful, however the `view` concept decides whether a view adapter will store independent copy of the range, or a reference to it. In particular lvalue of before mentioned optional<M> satisfies `viewable_range`, and is wrapped in `ref_view` when adapted:
This behavior is not unique to `optional`, and can occur for a user defined "view" that fails to satisfy `movable` since C++20. The C++26 changes to `optional` make it more prominent.
